title: A viewer signs in to Octave Web without anything a page's scripts can read
description: Serves PRODUCT.md: "A viewer signs in with a password" and "Access is enforced everywhere", and People rule 6: "Octave Web's sign-in is a cookie page scripts cannot read." Octave Web can't sign in to the new server, and it is where a TV is approved from until Octave's phone app exists (#301, #318).
acceptanceCriteria: A viewer signs in to Octave Web, served by the server, with a password; nothing the page's scripts can read signs anyone in.
A request from another site, or from another service on the same host name, can't act as the viewer; the protection does not rest on cookie rules alone.
Octave Web's sign-in is never accepted in a link or in place of a native app's sign-in.
Signing out ends it; it also ends after a stated idle time and a stated longest time.
Films, pictures and subtitles play in Chromium and Firefox with this sign-in, directly and behind a proxy that ends HTTPS.
The operator documentation says what address the server needs to itself and what a proxy must pass.
notes: Octave's design input on #301 is input to the design, not a fixed shape. The list of one's own sign-ins is stage 4 (devices).
